card.title: Gravitational potential energy
card.says: the energy stored by lifting mass $m$ to height $h$ above a chosen **reference level** ($h = 0$), where $g$ is the gravitational field strength. Only changes $\Delta E_p = m g \Delta h$ affect the motion.
card.from: the work needed to lift weight $m g$ steadily through vertical height $h$: $W = F h = m g h$.
card.useWhen: an object changes height near Earth's surface (so $g$ is nearly constant)—choose any convenient zero-height line and stick to it throughout the problem.
card.example: Lifting a $5\text{ kg}$ backpack onto a shelf $h = 2\text{ m}$ above the floor (with $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$) → $E_p = 5 \times 9.8 \times 2 = 98\text{ J}$.
card.analogy: Water held behind a hydroelectric dam stores height like money in a savings account; letting it drop cashes that height out into kinetic energy.
